label: doc_title
text: People and Events in the News of the World

label: text
text: Lord Oxford Asquith declared that the freedom of Great Britain was at stake in the fight between the Trade Unions and the Government. Rudyard Kipling, in poetry, urged the strikers to keep the peace. Ben Tillett, M.P., leader of the striking dock workers, was one of the biggest figures on the union side. Mr. Arthur Henderson, a Union leader, took his stand with the conservative element of Labour.

label: vision_footnote
text: Every one with the remotest connection with the Government or strikers in Great Britain was kept busy in May, Mrs. Stanley Baldwin, (top) wife of the Prime Minister, organised a motor transport corps to take women to work. Lady Cynthia Moseley, Socialist, raised money for the strikers' relief.

label: text
text: Baby Guy Stillman, central figure in the paternity dispute involved in the Stillman "Indian guide" divorce suit, will be taken into the home of his reconciled father and mother, Mrs. James A. Stillman, wife of the millionaire banker, announced after their return from the "second honeymoon" in Europe.

label: text
text: The Prince of Wales, visiting the House of Commons, smiled as Mr. George Buchanan, Labourite, said he would like to see the Throno abolished. Lord Burnham, declared that the Unions were trying to set up "a British super-Government." Sir Worthington-Evans, War Secretary, denied that mutiny would result in death sentences for soldiers and sailors. The Hon. John Whitley, M.P., started an independent move to end the strike.

label: text
text: Victor Napoleon, who bore the honorary title Prince Victor, the pretender to the throne of France, recently died in Brussels. Mr. J. L. Lewis, President of the United Mine Workers of America, conferred with Secretary of Labour Davis regarding the British strike. Mr. Oscar S. Straus, former U.S. Minister to Turkey, died in New York recently. Dr. Walter Seton was appointed as one of the food controllers of Great Britain during the strike.
